abstract: Gallup's February 2026 workplace survey of 23,717 employed U.S. adults documents accelerating AI adoption and its emerging workforce effects. Half of employed adults (50%) now use AI at least a few times yearly, with 28% using it weekly or more and 13% daily (up from 10% daily in 2024). Organizational integration has also increased, with 41% of employees reporting their organization has adopted AI tools (up 3 points quarterly). The survey reveals a significant divergence in workforce outcomes between AI-adopting and non-adopting organizations: 23% of employees at AI-adopting organizations report workforce reductions versus 16% at non-adopting organizations, a 7-percentage-point gap that represents one of the first large-scale survey measurements of differential displacement. AI-adopting organizations also show higher rates of disruptive workplace changes (27% vs. 17%) but simultaneously more hiring and expansion (34% vs. 28%). On productivity, 65% of AI users report improved productivity and efficiency, with 16% experiencing 'extremely positive' impacts, though only 1 in 10 strongly agree AI has transformed organizational workflows. Job security concerns remain elevated: 18% of all workers fear job elimination within five years from AI, rising to 23% in AI-adopting organizations.
keyFindings: 28% of employed US adults use AI weekly or more; 13% use daily (up from 10% in 2024); 50% use at least a few times yearly.
23% of employees at AI-adopting organizations report workforce reductions versus 16% at non-adopting organizations — a 7pp differential displacement signal.
41% of employees report their organization has adopted AI tools, up 3 percentage points from the prior quarter.
65% of AI users report improved productivity, but only 10% strongly agree AI has transformed organizational workflows, suggesting adoption outpaces structural change.
18% of all workers fear AI-driven job elimination within 5 years, rising to 23% at AI-adopting organizations.
methodology: Probability-based web survey of 23,717 employed U.S. adults conducted February 4-19, 2026, via Gallup Panel members. Margin of error ±0.9 percentage points at 95% confidence level. Design effect of 2.02. Results weighted for demographics to represent the employed U.S. adult population. Gallup Panel uses address-based sampling methodology for probability-based recruitment.
qualifiers: The 23% vs. 16% workforce reduction comparison between AI-adopting and non-adopting organizations could reflect reverse causality — organizations undergoing restructuring may be more likely to adopt AI as part of cost-cutting, rather than AI causing the reductions. Self-reported AI usage may overcount or undercount depending on how respondents define 'AI.' The survey captures perceptions and self-reports, not verified organizational employment data. The 'AI-adopting organization' classification is based on employee perception, which may not align with actual organizational AI deployment. Web panel surveys, even probability-based, may underrepresent certain demographics.
